title: Top K Frequent Elements
corePattern: Frequency Counting + Top-K Selection (Hash Map with Sorting / Heap / Bucket Sort)
interviewTips: Clarify: can answer be in any order? Is k always valid (1 <= k <= distinct count)? Are ties broken arbitrarily?
Trade-off: Sorting is simplest O(n log n), min-heap of size k is O(n log k) and good for streaming, bucket sort is optimal O(n) when frequencies bounded by n.
Edge cases: k equals number of distinct elements, n=1, all frequencies equal, negative numbers, large n with small k.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Count + Sort
approaches.intuition: Count how many times each number appears, then sort distinct numbers by frequency descending and take first k.
approaches.theory: Use hash map to get frequency in O(n). There are m <= n distinct keys. Sorting m pairs by frequency costs O(m log m). Slicing top k gives answer. Simple and correct because ordering by frequency directly defines top k frequent elements.

timeComplexity.explanation: O(n) to count, O(m log m) to sort m distinct elements where m <= n, so worst O(n log n).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Hash map stores up to n distinct counts plus array of pairs for sorting.

edgeCases: n=1, k=1 returns the single element
All elements same frequency, any k of them valid
k equals distinct count returns all distinct keys

approaches.name: Approach 2: Count + Min-Heap of Size K
approaches.intuition: We only need top k, not full order. Keep a min-heap of size k keyed by frequency so the smallest among top k is at the top and can be evicted.
approaches.theory: Count frequencies in O(n). Iterate over m distinct entries, push (freq, num) into min-heap. If heap size exceeds k, pop smallest. Invariant: heap always holds k largest frequencies seen so far. At end heap contains top k. Pop to output. Heap operations are O(log k) over m entries.

timeComplexity.explanation: O(n) counting + O(m log k) heap pushes/pops for m distinct elements. Better than sorting when k << m.

spaceComplexity.explanation: O(m) for hash map + O(k) for heap, overall O(n).

edgeCases: k=1 keeps only max frequency via heap size 1
k equals distinct count: heap never pops
Large n with small k shows best speedup vs sorting

approaches.name: Approach 3: Bucket Sort by Frequency
approaches.intuition: Frequency of any value is between 1 and n. Use frequency as index into buckets to avoid comparison sorting.
approaches.theory: Count frequencies O(n). Create buckets array of size n+1 where buckets[f] holds all numbers with frequency f. This is counting-sort over frequency domain. Then scan buckets from n down to 1 collecting numbers until k collected. Each number placed once and scanned once, so linear. Correct because higher index means higher frequency.

timeComplexity.explanation: Counting O(n), distributing into buckets O(m), scanning buckets O(n). Total linear.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Hash map O(m) plus buckets holding m elements total plus O(n) bucket array.

steps: scan i=6..4 empty, i=3 => take 1 => res [1]

edgeCases: Single distinct value with freq n uses buckets[n]
All distinct (freq 1): buckets[1] has n items, take any k
k=distinct count requires scanning down to freq 1
